title: Deferred Revenue Adjustments for Dedicated Capacity Commitments
author: Aisha Patel
content:
SUMMARY
This document defines the policy and operational procedure for calculating, adjusting, and journal-ing deferred revenue associated with Dedicated Capacity (reserved GPU pools and monthly/annual commit contracts). It covers common exceptions, change-of-scope events, refunds/credits, mid-term amendments, and the required finance and legal approvals. The goal is to ensure revenue recognition is accurate, auditable, and aligned with ASC 606 principles and Redwood’s internal revrec playbooks.

SCOPE
Applies to: 
- All new and existing Dedicated Capacity contracts (monthly and annual commitments) sold through self-serve, sales, or partners.
- Finance, Legal, Revenue Ops, Billing, Procurement, and Account Management teams involved in contract lifecycle.
Excludes: Hosted API metered usage (handled by standard token-based revrec processes) and marketplace third-party reseller transactions (handled per partner agreement).

KEY DEFINITIONS
- Dedicated Commitment: A customer purchase that reserves compute capacity for a fixed commit term (e.g., 12 months).
- Billable Commitment: Portion of the commitment invoiced up-front or on a fixed cadence.
- Deferred Revenue: Liability recorded for cash received but not yet recognized as revenue.
- Performance Obligation: The contractual promise to make Dedicated capacity available and supported.
- Usage Tail Events: Customer overage or underutilization events that require billing adjustments or credits.

POLICY PRINCIPLES
1) Revenue recognition follows ASC 606: identify obligations, determine transaction price (including discounts/credits), allocate, and recognize as the obligation is satisfied. For Dedicated Capacity, revenue is recognized ratably over the term unless a distinct performance pattern is documented and approved.
2) Material contract amendments (term changes, capacity tier changes, or material price adjustments > 10% of remaining contract value) require a remeasurement of the transaction price and a new allocation schedule.
3) Refunds and credits that result in an effective decrease to the transaction price are recognized as adjustments to deferred revenue prospectively unless they correspond to previously recognized revenue and thus require retrospective adjustment.
4) All deferred revenue journal entries must be supported by a revenue schedule stored in the RevOps system and cross-referenced to the contract in the CLM (Contract Lifecycle Management) tool.

ROLES & OWNERSHIP
- Revenue Ops: primary owner for generating the initial revrec schedule and posting recurring recognition entries.
- Finance: review and approve month-end manual adjustments, run accruals and closing checklist.
- Legal: approve contract amendments and confirm interpretation of change-of-scope language.
- Billing/AR: issue invoices, process refunds/credits, and update payment status.
- Account Management/Customer Success: validate service changes with customers and provide change documentation.

STANDARD PROCEDURE FOR NEW DEDICATED CONTRACTS
1. Contract capture (Sales & CLM)
   - Ensure the CLM entry includes: start_date, term_months, committed_capacity_tier, price_schedule, payment_terms, SLA credits, and amendment rules.
2. Initial invoicing and booking (Billing & RevOps)
   - If customer prepays or pays an upfront deposit: create a deferred revenue liability equal to the prepayment.
   - If invoiced on a monthly/quarterly cadence: invoice as per payment_terms and book receivable; create deferred liability for portion not yet earned.
3. Revrec schedule generation (RevOps)
   - Default recognition: straight-line (daily) over the contract term.
   - If justified: apply alternate recognition (e.g., usage-weighted) only after Finance + Legal sign-off.
4. Storage & traceability
   - Store the schedule record in the RevOps system with a link to the CLM contract ID and invoice references.

HANDLING MID-TERM AMENDMENTS (CHANGE OF SCOPE)
Overview: Amendments fall into three buckets: non-material administrative changes, material prospective changes, and termination/early-exit. Each bucket has different accounting treatments.
Procedure: 
1) Classify the amendment (Legal)
   - Non-material administrative (e.g., billing address) \u2014 no revrec remeasurement.
   - Material prospective (e.g., increase/decrease capacity, extend term) \u2014 remeasure transaction price.
   - Termination/early-exit \u2014 evaluate for immediate recognition of remaining deferred revenue less any refund liabilities.
2) Remeasurement (Finance + RevOps)
   - Calculate incremental or decremental consideration attributable to remaining performance obligations.
   - Determine whether control transferred at a point in time or over time for the new obligations.
3) Journal approach
   - Prospective increases: allocate additional consideration to remaining term and recognize ratably unless another pattern is justified.
   - Prospective decreases: reduce deferred revenue on remaining term; if previously recognized revenue is affected, apply retrospective adjustment and document rationale.
4) Approvals
   - All material remeasurements require Finance sign-off and Legal concurrence before posting.

EXCEPTIONS: UNDERUTILIZATION & CREDITS
When utilization is materially below committed levels and a contract prescribes credits or refunds, apply the following: 
- If credit is contractually guaranteed (e.g., minimum usage SLA), treat as variable consideration constrained until realized and record as reduction to transaction price when it is probable that a significant reversal will not occur.
- If billing credit is an account-level concession (sales agreed to a makeup or credit after the fact), record as a reduction of unearned revenue if the customer has not been provided the performance in the past; otherwise, treat as contra-revenue.

DETAILED JOURNAL ENTRIES (EXAMPLES)
Example 1: Annual prepay for $120,000 for 12-month dedicated commit, straight-line recognition.
- On receipt (initial booking): Debit Cash $120,000; Credit Deferred Revenue $120,000.
- Monthly recognition (end of month): Debit Deferred Revenue $10,000; Credit Revenue $10,000.

Example 2: Mid-term capacity downgrade on month 6, original contract $120k/year, remaining unearned $60k, new remaining consideration for remainder term $30k (customer refund not issued, but reduction applies).
- Remeasure: reduce deferred revenue by $30,000. If refund issued $30k: Debit Deferred Revenue $30,000; Credit Cash $30,000. If no cash refund and reduction applied to future invoices: Debit Deferred Revenue $30,000; Credit Revenue $30,000 (if applicable) with a memo to note method and approval.

CONTROL CHECKS & MONTH-END CLOSE TASKS
Finance month-end checklist (revrec-specific):
- Reconcile RevOps schedule totals to general ledger deferred revenue balance.
- Review all contract amendments processed in period and confirm remeasurement approvals attached.
- Confirm that any refunds/credits processed by Billing have corresponding GL entries and CLM amendment links.
- Run exception report: contracts with > 15% variance between expected utilization and invoiced amounts.

APPROVALS & ESCALATION MATRIX
- < $25k adjustment: Revenue Ops + Finance Controller sign-off.
- $25k 3 $250k adjustment: Revenue Ops + Finance Lead + Legal notification.
- > $250k adjustment or material contract amendment: Finance Director + Legal Counsel + VP Revenue approval.
- Disputed customer-initiated changes: escalate to Sales Leadership and Legal for negotiation; do not post revenue adjustments until approvals complete.

OPERATIONS: SYSTEMS, FIELDS & REQUIRED DOCUMENTATION
Required fields on CLM and RevOps records: contract_id, customer_id, start_date, end_date, committed_capacity, invoice_ids, payment_terms, amendment_log_id, revrec_schedule_id, revrec_method ("straight_line"/"usage_weighted"), accounting_memo_id.
Sample table: 
| Field | Purpose | Owner | Required? |
| contract_id | Primary CLM identifier | Sales/Legal | Yes |
| revrec_schedule_id | Link to RevOps schedule | Revenue Ops | Yes |
| revrec_method | Recognition pattern | Finance | Yes |
| amendment_log_id | Link to amendment documentation | Legal | Conditional |

SAMPLE ACCOUNTING JSON FOR MANUAL IMPORT (RevOps)
{
  "contract_id": "CLM-2026-1293",
  "customer_id": "CUST-9021",
  "start_date": "2026-01-01",
  "end_date": "2026-12-31",
  "total_consideration": "120000",
  "unearned_balance": "120000",
  "revrec_method": "straight_line",
  "period_amount": "10000"
}

REPORTING & KPIS
- Monthly deferred revenue aging by contract and by customer.
- Quarterly material amendment roll-forward (value and count).
- Overage/underutilization credits as % of committed value.
- Time-to-approval for material amendment (goal: < 7 business days).

AUDIT & DOCUMENT RETENTION
- Retain contract and amendment documentation, approval emails, and RevOps schedule worksheets for 7 years.
- During audits, provide the revrec trail: CLM entry, RevOps schedule, invoices, GL entries, and approval memos.

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (SHORT)
Q: When do we recognize the remainder of deferred revenue on early termination?
A: If the termination results in no further performance obligation and there is no refund obligation, remaining deferred revenue is recognized immediately; if a refund obligation exists, recognize net of the refund liability per ASC 606 guidance and consult Finance Director.

Q: How are SLA credits represented in revrec?
A: SLA credits are treated as variable consideration and recorded as a reduction of transaction price when it is probable that a significant reversal will not occur.

APPENDIX: TEMPLATES & CHECKLISTS
- Remeasurement approval template (required fields): amendment_id, rationale, quantitative_impact, finance_signoff, legal_signoff, coo_notified.
- Month-end revrec checklist (ticklist): schedule reconciliation, new amendments review, aged exception report, key GL variance notes.
